App.Packing: Packing in linked entries: {done} of {total} compendiums
App.Summary: {assets} files used, {copied} will be copied ({size}). {issues} broken links.

Details.Intro: The adventure and the files it uses are packed into a module ZIP. Other GMs install it like any module and import the adventure from its compendium.

Id.Label: Module ID
Id.Hint: Lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores. It becomes the folder name and must be unique on the servers it is installed on.

Title.Label: Title
Title.Hint: Shown in the module list. The compendium gets the same name.

Url.Label: Project URL
Url.Hint: Optional. A website or repository for the module.

Details.License: Only share files you are allowed to share. Maps, tokens and art from other modules or purchased packs usually may not be redistributed: leave them out and list the module as a dependency instead.

world.Label: World files
world.Hint: Files in this world's folder. Copied into the module.

data.Label: User data files
data.Hint: Files in your user data folder. Copied into the module.

storage.Label: Cloud storage
storage.Hint: Files on your S3 or Forge storage. Copied into the module, if the storage allows the download.

module.Label: Files from other modules
module.Hint: Not copied by default: these modules become dependencies. Only copy files you are allowed to share.

external.Label: Web links
external.Hint: Files on other websites. Kept as links by default. Copying works only if the website allows it.

core.Label: Foundry files
core.Hint: Part of Foundry VTT. Every server has them.

system.Label: Game system files
system.Hint: Part of the game system, which the module requires.

Status.missing: Not found: the path stays unchanged

PackIn.Label: Linked content
PackIn.Hint: The adventure links to these documents and compendium entries. Tick a source to pack its linked entries into the adventure: they are imported with it, links point to the imported copies, and the source is no longer needed for them. Entries those entries link to in ticked sources are packed in too, however deep the links go. World documents and world compendiums are ticked by default. Only pack in content you are allowed to share.
PackIn.Toggle: Pack linked entries into the adventure
PackIn.NotAvailable: This compendium is not available in this world.
PackIn.NotPackable: Entries of this type can't be part of an adventure.
PackIn.SystemPack: Part of the game system (for example SRD content). Never packed in: every GM using the module has it, so these links keep working.
PackIn.Limited: Packing in stopped at {max} entries. Some links still point into the compendiums.

Dependencies.Label: Module dependencies
Dependencies.Hint: Modules the adventure takes files or compendium content from are required by default. Modules that only stored data on its documents are recommended. A module the adventure only needs for its files is not listed once you copy all of them. What you choose here by hand is kept.
Dependencies.None: The adventure needs no other modules.
Dependencies.Inactive: Installed, but not active in this world. Activate it to check and pack in its compendium links.
Dependencies.AllCopied: all files copied into the module

missingDocument.Label: Documents not in the adventure
missingDocument.Hint: Links, tokens or notes point to world documents that are not part of the adventure. Add them to the adventure to keep the links working.

worldPack.Label: World compendiums
worldPack.Hint: Links into compendiums of this world. Other GMs don't have them.

sourcePack.Label: The adventure's own compendium
sourcePack.Hint: Links into the compendium the adventure is stored in. The new module has its own compendium, so these links break.

unknownPack.Label: Unknown compendiums
unknownPack.Hint: Links into compendiums that are not available in this world.

Result.Title: Module exported
Result.Downloaded: Your browser saves the ZIP to its downloads folder.
Result.Failures: {count} files could not be downloaded. Their paths were left unchanged:
Result.Install: To install it, extract the ZIP into the modules folder of a Foundry user data folder, enable the module, and import the adventure from its compendium. The README in the ZIP says the same for the GMs you share it with.

Errors.GMOnly: Only a GM can export adventures.
Errors.InvalidId: The module ID may only contain lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores, and must start with a letter or number.
Errors.ReservedId: This module ID is already used by the game system or by Adventure to Module.
Errors.LoadFailed: The adventure could not be loaded: {error}

Warnings.IdInstalled: A module with the ID "{id}" is installed here. Installing the ZIP on this server replaces it.
Warnings.LargeInMemory: The files to copy add up to about {size}. This browser can't save directly to disk, so it keeps the whole ZIP in memory until the download starts, which can crash the tab. Chrome, Edge and the Foundry app save directly. Export anyway?
